definition: A typed Mapping projects explicitly supplied values into declared target fields; it neither constructs an Entity nor evaluates an implicit Calculation.
v2: The closed body contains description, target and typed_contract. The closed typed contract contains schema_version, ontology_mapping, inputs, target, fields and total. Inputs are ordered unique typed name slots; fields contain target, value and default. Value expressions reuse the typed value algebra with canonical decimal UInt64 literals.
bindings: Input and target selectors resolve through the checked graph and exact field model. Field expressions preserve ontology property identities. Complete and partial projections are explicit. Named Entity and Value Object values retain their declared meaning.
defaults: V1 fallback applies to absent source properties only, not explicit null. V2 default is a lazy explicit fallback for a nullable expression; its type must agree with the target. No automatic calculation, coercion or optional traversal is inserted.
effects: Normalize complete declared inputs as inert data, project frozen typed values, and return a fully consumed immutable field projection. Do not perform IO, lookup, factory construction, invariant execution or hidden dependency calls.
representation: TypeScript bound-mapping/v1 candidate form: static arrow provider plus immutable source/signature/target/provider descriptor. Native compiler, independent observation and behavioral mutation evidence are required.
compatibility: Existing source schemas and default generator output remain unchanged. Typed Mapping v2 requires an explicit configured generator; unsupported legacy entry points reject before producing artifacts. Historical parser source selections remain immutable; a separate successor records changed source bytes.
